subject: Post-call: BrightMed discovery — privacy/logging checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightmed.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: BrightMed discovery — privacy/logging checklist & next steps

Hi Elena / Ian —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same checklist and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Regulatory requirement: must demonstrate HIPAA-safe handling for patient-identifiable data and provide an auditable retention record.
- Current blocker: security team will not accept raw prompt/response logging to a third-party; any logged data must be redacted or stored in your VPC.
- Latency constraint: clinical UI needs median response <150ms for autocomplete-style queries; some heavier prompt workflows can tolerate ~500ms.

Current stack we heard
- Frontend: React app behind internal load balancer.
- Data platform: Snowflake + S3 (encrypted, customer-managed KMS).
- Internal infra: EKS clusters in AWS us-east-1, corporate VPC.
- Existing ML: a small on-prem transformer for internal experiments; looking to move inference to a managed, auditable runtime.

Success criteria for a pilot
1) No raw PHI leaves customer VPC unless explicit encryption + audit chain.
2) Configurable log retention (options: 0 days, 30 days, 90 days, 365 days) with immutable audit logs exportable to your SIEM.
3) Demonstrable redaction pipeline (PII/PHI redaction pre-store) and a way to disable prompt logging entirely.
4) End-to-end latency within targets for the UI use-case.

Security constraints you emphasized
- Redaction: must be able to automatically remove patient identifiers before any persistent logging.
- Auditability: immutable access + action logs for 12 months (potentially 7 years depending on use-case) with export capabilities.
- Key management: integration with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest.
- No external model training on your data; strict no-usage for model improvements unless explicitly opt-in.

Proposed immediate next steps
- We will send our short security one-pager and SOC2 excerpts (attached quicksheet). Rafael will follow with a draft MAP and estimated pilot pricing.
- Schedule a 45-min architecture review (security + infra folks). Can we target Wed 11/12 or Thu 11/13?
- Deliver a short prototype plan showing: private deployment (VPC), redaction hook example, and retention policy options.

Attachments: redwood-security-quicksheet.pdf, MAP-draft-brightmed.xlsx (draft)

If that all looks right I’ll: (a) request a security contact and questionnaire owner from your side, (b) lock the architecture review time, and (c) share a MAP draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Lead, West
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Dr. Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightmed.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ian Cho <ian.cho@brightmed.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightMed discovery — privacy/logging checklist & next steps

Thanks, Sergio — this is a helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) On redaction: can Redwood support token-level redaction before storage? We need proof that patient identifiers (name, MRN, DOB) are not recoverable after redaction.
2) Retention windows: compliance would ideally like a 30-day default but the ability to extend to 7 years for audit cases. Is that flexible?
3) Architecture review: Wed 11/12 10:30am PT works for our security architect (Ian) and me.

Also, please include any sample architecture diagrams and an NDA — our legal team prefers an NDA before we circulate internal diagrams.

Appreciate it —

Elena
Director of Clinical Data & Integrations
BrightMed
elena.morales@brightmed.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightmed.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightMed discovery — privacy/logging checklist & next steps

Elena —

Great — Wed 11/12 10:30am PT is on our side. Quick answers inline: 

1) Token-level redaction: yes — Redwood Private supports configurable pre-store redaction hooks. We can show an example that strips identified PHI fields and hashes or blanks them before any persistent storage. We will bring a short demo of a redaction pipeline that you can run in a staging VPC.

2) Retention windows: flexible. Our platform supports per-tenant retention policies and we can set defaults and overrides per workspace. We will surface export tooling for audit use cases (S3 export of logs + audit trail).

3) NDA and diagrams: attaching a short security quicksheet now. I’ll ask Legal to share our standard mutual NDA (if that helps speed things).

Next actions on our side: Rafael will attach a draft MAP with milestones and Marissa will send the calendar invite for Wed. Rafael — I’m assigning the MAP draft and a simple SOW template for BrightMed (cc’d).

Thanks,
Sergio
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Dr. Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft + pilot scope (initial)

Elena / Sergio —

Attaching a very light MAP (MAP-draft-brightmed.xlsx) and a starter SOW (SOW-template-redwood.docx). High level pilot scope:
- 6-week POC: private deployment in customer VPC, redaction pipeline, retention config, 1 model up to 4k tokens.
- Deliverables: architecture diagram, runbook for audit exports, redaction test cases, performance report (latency percentiles).
- Estimated list price for pilot: $32k (one-time) + $X/month for reserved capacity (TBD pending sizing).

Open items we need from BrightMed:
- Security contact and point person for questionnaire.
- Confirmation on retention policy target ranges (30/90/365/7yrs).
- Example prompts or redaction rules you want validated.

I can update MAP with your legal/finance preferences after we get the NDA in place.

Rafael
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
